name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *only* new-contributor PRs for two weeks. This tests the tool’s edge-case catching without risking friction on core contributors—trade-off is missing bugs in veteran PRs. If it performs well, we expand to all PRs; if not, we scrap it without disrupting the team.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t missing bugs in veteran PRs—it’s normalizing noise so reviewers ignore *all* PR-Agent output, even when it flags something critical. A better alternative is running it in shadow mode on *random* PRs (10-20%) to avoid bias toward new contributors while still stress-testing edge cases. Settle it by tracking reviewer response rates to PR-Agent comments over two weeks—if engagement drops, the experiment fails.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for one week first, then filter results to compare noise levels between new and veteran contributors—this gives us data to decide whether bias toward new contributors is justified without doubling the test period. If noise is similar across groups, we skip the new-contributor-only phase entirely and save two weeks of partial testing.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for one week first. This gives us a full baseline of noise across the board—no blind spots, no bias toward new contributors. The trade-off is slightly higher reviewer fatigue upfront, but it prevents us from normalizing ignored warnings later. If the noise is manageable, we’ll expand to targeted testing; if not, we’ll scrap it before wasting weeks on a flawed approach.
